sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 5.4% a year from $114 billion in FY2016 to $184 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F177], but the path was a commodity cycle, not a trend.
Revenue fell 32.5% in FY2020 to $94.5 billion [F5][D153], then rose 64.7% in FY2021 and 51.5% in FY2022 to $236 billion [F6][F7][D192][D232].
The FY2022 surge came from higher upstream realizations and downstream margins [P57], and the FY2023 fall of 16.5% to $197 billion [F8][D274] followed lower realizations and downstream margins [P44].
Revenue then declined three straight years, to $193 billion in FY2024 and $184 billion in FY2025 [F9][F10][D316][D358], on lower crude and refined product prices [P17].
Chevron U.S.A. Inc. supplied 75.1% of FY2025 revenue [D402] and its 5.3% decline subtracted 3.9pp from growth [D403][D404].
Tengizchevroil was 11.6% of FY2025 revenue [D418] and its 16.5% growth added 1.5pp [D419][D420], while the Affiliated Entity fell 9.3% and subtracted 0.6pp [D426][D427].
The FY2025 revenue decline came mainly from lower crude oil and refined product prices, partly offset by higher sales volumes [P17].
Operating costs fell 3.4% against a 4.6% revenue decline [D373][D358], so there was no operating leverage and net income fell 30.5% [D359].
Diluted EPS fell 31.8% [D361], slightly more than net income, because the diluted share count rose 2.1% [D374].
Net margin was 6.7% in FY2025 [F30], below its 7.9% window median [D613] and far under the 15.1% FY2022 high [D612].
The 2.5pp net margin decline in FY2025 [D369] came from higher upstream depreciation, lower realizations and higher operating costs [P9].
Cost of revenue fell to 57.2% of revenue from 58.8% [D338][D296], and SG&A rose to 2.7% from 2.4% [D340][D298].
The effective tax rate rose to 36.8% from 35.5% [D345][D303], widening the gap between operating and net margin.
Net margin ranked in the 33rd percentile against six energy peers, whose median was 10.2% [D631][D632].
Operating cash flow of $33.9 billion was 2.76x net income [F60][F20][D346], above the 1.10x window median [D622].
Free cash flow was $16.6 billion, an 8.8% margin [F80][D343], against a 8.9% window median [D616].
Operating cash flow rose 7.8% [D362] as higher TCO distributions and legacy Hess assets more than offset lower commodity prices [P6].
Capex of $17.3 billion was 9.2% of revenue [F70][D342] and 0.86x D&A [D348].
Net cash was $4.0 billion at FY2025, or 2.1% of revenue [D351][D352], after net debt of $156 million in FY2024 [D309].
That net cash position ranked in the 83rd percentile against six energy peers, whose median was -7.7% of revenue [D637][D638].
Buybacks of $12.1 billion plus dividends of $12.8 billion totaled $24.8 billion [X132][X142][D353], 149.7% of free cash flow [D354].
The diluted share count still rose 2.1% [D374], so per-share results did not benefit from the buybacks.
Revenue has fallen for three straight years, from $197 billion in FY2023 to $184 billion in FY2025 [F8][F10][R1].
Buybacks and dividends exceeded free cash flow in each of FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 [D270][D312][D354][R4], a payout that depends on the cycle.
The revenue table is a later recast for FY2018 through FY2025, so growth rates mix two presentations [R3][F10][X10].
Non-US downstream was 34.9% of revenue and fell 13.1% in FY2025 [D517][D518][R6].
Watch net margin against the 7.9% window median [D613]; a print below it in the FY2026 10-K would extend the FY2025 decline [D369].
Watch free cash flow against the $16.6 billion FY2025 level [F80]; a fall below it would strain the 149.7% payout ratio [D354].
Watch capex against the $18-19 billion 2026 guidance [P4]; spending above it would pressure the 8.8% free cash flow margin [D343].
